thread:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout model-runtime-v2.1.3 started at 2026-03-15T14:02Z. Automated monitors: p95 latency +420ms, p99 +2.3s, 5xx rate jumped 0.2% -> 4.8% on canary nodes. Alert CI-2795012345.

incident-bot: Declaring incident SEV2 due to elevated 5xx/timeouts. Paging ops-oncall. Incident channel: #incidents. Runbook: /runbooks/timeout-regression.

ops-oncall (Maya): I'm on it. Initial check: errors are concentrated behind the inference gateway in eu-west-1, mostly 502/504 and some 503. Canary is ~5% of traffic. Rolling back suggested if root cause quick to confirm.

eng-sre (Ravi): Looking at traces now — I'm seeing long upstream waits on the runtime pool. A few traces show request queued ~1.8s then backend timeout. Possible connection pooling regression in v2.1.3.

runtime-team (Lina): We shipped a change to connection keepalive + aggressive idle eviction in v2.1.3 to free sockets faster. Hypothesis: new eviction + reduced pool size causing connection churn under burst -> timeouts.

customer-success (Tom): CS queue: 6 customers reported 502s in last 15m, biggest: AcmeCorp (EU traffic) saw ~30% request failures for 2-3 minutes. They're asking for ETA.

ops-oncall (Maya): Can we mitigate without full rollback? Options: 1) increase pool size / disable eviction flag; 2) revert to v2.1.2; 3) shift traffic off canary. Which is fastest?

runtime-team (Lina): Quick toggle: set ENV RUNTIME_KEEPALIVE_EVICTION=off on canary nodes and bump pool to 256. That should restore steady state in <2min once config reloads. If not, rollback.

eng-sre (Ravi): I'm hitting the canary hosts with a small load reproduction script. Attaching a failing span:

```
[14:05:12Z] ERROR request_id=trc_7b3a9c upstream_timeout: context deadline exceeded after 4.5s
span: gateway->runtime.connect (wait 2.8s) -> runtime.process (1.2s) -> gateway.send (0.5s)
```

ops-oncall (Maya): Applying the ENV change to canary pool now (kubectl set env deployment/model-runtime CANARY=true RUNTIME_KEEPALIVE_EVICTION=off -n inference). Pushing patch.

deploy-bot: Patch applied to 3 canary pods at 14:07:23Z. Restart sequence initiated.

eng-sre (Ravi): After restart, p95 dropped by ~180ms within one minute, 5xx fell to 1.6%. Still higher than baseline. Monitoring for 5 more minutes.

product-ops (Ana): Notifying support playbook: send templated message to impacted customers, note temporary degraded behavior. Tom, can you send something concise?

customer-success (Tom): Sending ACME note now: "We're aware of transient 502/504s affecting inference in EU; engineers are mitigating; rollback in progress if required. We'll update in 30 min."

ops-oncall (Maya): p99 still elevated on longer sequences; seeing occasional 504s traced to socket resets. Lina, can we also increase keepalive timeout?

runtime-team (Lina): Doing that now: set KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT=120s on canary. Patch applied at 14:12Z.

eng-sre (Ravi): Nice, p99 dropped ~600ms after the second change. 5xx ~0.6% now. But some requests still hit backend queueing for >1s.

ops-oncall (Maya): Given partial recovery but customer impact, I'd like to avoid a full rollback if we can stabilize. However if 5xx >1% for next 10 min we rollback. Agreed?

eng-sre (Ravi): Agreed. I'll keep digging into connection histograms and backend concurrency. If we see further regression I'll initiate rollback.

incident-bot: Pager: oncall escalation threshold crossed (5xx >1% sustained 5m). Paging oncall-next (Jules) for potential handoff.

oncall-next (Jules): I'm here, catching up. Summary?

ops-oncall (Maya): Quick: canary deploy v2.1.3 caused connection churn due to eviction change. We patched keepalive eviction off and increased timeout + pool size. Partial recovery. Monitoring. Customers notified. If we don't reach baseline soon, rollback will be performed.

oncall-next (Jules): Good. If you opt to rollback, prefer /rollout undo to last-stable to preserve config. Also capture a sample pod for postmortem.

eng-sre (Ravi): Traces show correlation with request size >8k tokens for p99 spikes. Gateway is opening many concurrent upstream connections for long-running requests; pool exhaustion appears at the canary node level.

ops-oncall (Maya): Quick mitigation: enable temporary circuit-breaker at gateway for requests >12s to fail fast and reduce queueing. Can we flip that?

runtime-team (Lina): Gateway flag set: MAX_REQUEST_DURATION_MS=12000 -> requests over limit return 524 quick. Applied at 14:28Z. This should reduce queue buildup from extreme tails.

eng-sre (Ravi): After circuit-breaker, backend queue length dropped by ~70%, p99 converging toward baseline. 5xx now at 0.3%.

customer-success (Tom): Sending follow-up to impacted customers: "We deployed a fix that reduced error rates; some degraded responses may still occur — ongoing monitoring. ETA for resolution 30-45m."

product-ops (Ana): Noting customer's business impact for severity assessment. ACME reported 30% failure spike for ~6 minutes; will open a customer incident and flag for credits if SLA breached.

ops-oncall (Maya): Since mitigations (disable eviction + keepalive bump + gateway circuit) restored service to near-baseline and root cause is a config regression in v2.1.3, runtime-team: please prepare a patch that reworks eviction logic and add a safety gate for pool size. We'll schedule a controlled re-deploy after tests.

runtime-team (Lina): On it. Will create PR with feature flag defaulted off and add unit + soak test.

eng-sre (Ravi): Capture: trace ids trc_7b3a9c, trc_9d8f21, trc_f44c11 for postmortem. Also saved kube logs: pod model-runtime-canary-2 stderr snippet.

ops-oncall (Maya): Rolling note: no full rollback executed. Canary paused at 5% until runtime patch confirmed. We will not continue rollout.

incident-bot: Incident state: Mitigated -> Monitoring. SEV2 remains open for postmortem.

oncall-next (Jules): I'll take the handoff at 15:45Z. Maya, leave any outstanding action items in the incident doc: /incidents/CI-2795012345.

ops-oncall (Maya): Handoff: "Mitigated via config toggles (RUNTIME_KEEPALIVE_EVICTION=off, KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT=120s), gateway circuit-breaker enabled, canary paused. Actions: runtime PR, add load test for keepalive eviction, customer outreach follow-ups." Adding notes to doc now.

customer-success (Tom): I'll follow up with ACME and send an SLA update once postmortem available.

eng-sre (Ravi): Will draft postmortem with timeline + technical root cause. Putting traces and logs in the doc.

oncall-next (Jules): Acknowledged. If any regression recurs, page me immediately. I'll continue monitoring until 18:00Z.

ops-oncall (Maya): Thanks all — moving to watch mode. Closing live coordination in this thread, continuing updates in incident doc. :white_check_mark:
